To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sphere hierarchy can be used efficiently to detect collisions of deformable necklaces and that the power diagram can be used for certain self-collisions.

(a) a bounding sphere hierarchy can be used to detect collisions and self-collisions for a necklace in a sub-quadratic amount of time, and (b) the power diagram, when used with additional mechanisms, can detect self-colliding necklaces.

(1) a bounding volume hierarchy of spheres is a good data structure for collision detection of deformable necklaces, (2) the power diagram is also useful for this problem, (3) both data structures can be efficiently computed and maintained, and (4) both can be used for self-collision detection as well.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, analysis, and implementation of geometric structures that can be maintained efficiently under deformation.
developing geometric structures that are suitable to be used in physical simulations of deformable necklaces.
a new class of objects that are useful in modeling deformable linear structures.

our proposed methods are efficient, practical, and easy to implement, and can be used to detect collisions and self-collisions between necklaces and other objects, and among necklaces, respectively.
the sphere hierarchy is a good choice for detecting collisions of two necklaces and the power diagram is a good choice to detect self-collision in a single necklace.
